questions.solution:
Broad money includes all forms of money in circulation, including cash and bank deposits, while narrow money only includes the most liquid forms of money.

· M1 money includes cash and demand deposits.

· M2 money includes M1 money (cash and demand deposits) along with savings deposits held in banks and post office savings deposits.

· M3 money includes M1 money (cash and demand deposits), M2 money (M1 + savings deposits), time deposits with banks, and other deposits with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

· M4 money includes M3 money (M1 + M2 + time deposits + other deposits with the RBI) as well as all deposits held with post office savings banks.

Among above four type of money forms, M1 is narrowest form of money and M2 is narrow form of money.

questions.solution:
Sentence R comes first as it introduces the subject of the passage 'McArthur Wheeler' who robbed two banks in broad daylight. Sentence Q comes next as mentions that he didn't even hide his identity and was not scared to show his face while robbing the bank. Sentence S follows and mentions how the police tried to catch him and sentence P concludes the passage by informing that he was caught within an hour. So, the correct order is RQSP.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Isn't knowled g e supposed to make life sweeter and happier?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Isn't knowledge supposed to make life sweeter and happier?
questions.solution:
Knowledge - facts, information, and skills acquired through experience or education; the theoretical or practical understanding of a subject.

Wisdom - the quality of having experience, knowledge, and good judgement; the quality of being wise.

So, both words are synonyms of each other.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Curriculum - the subjects comprising a course of study in a school or college.

Profession - a university academic of the highest rank; the holder of a university chair.

Superiority - the quality of being better than average, or better than others of the same type.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The man which was present at the meeting spoke against the chairperson.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The man which was present at the meeting spoke against the chairperson.
questions.solution:
The relative pronoun 'which' is not used for humans. So, options a) and b) are incorrect. The relative pronoun 'whom' is used to refer to the object of the sentence, whereas 'the man' here is the subject, so the relative pronoun 'who' should replace 'which' in the underlined phrase. The phrase in option d) represents this rectification.

The correct sentence is: The man who was present at the meeting spoke against the chairperson.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to complete the given sentence. They were not able to get the item from the store because it was ________.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to complete the given sentence.

They were not able to get the item from the store because it was ________.
questions.solution:
In fashion - popular and considered to be attractive at the time in question.

In vain - without success or a result.

Out of stock - (of goods) unavailable for immediate sale in a shop.

On leave - absent from duty with permission.

The sentence discusses that the subject could not buy the item from the store. Among the given options, only 'out of stock' fits contextually and gives the meaning that the item was not available in the store and hence they couldn't buy it.

The complete sentence is: They were not able to get the item from the store because it was out of stock.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. I must tell you that it all went pear-shaped after you left the meeting in the middle.
questions.questionHtml:

questions.solution:
Go/went pear-shaped - to go wrong.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word 'dwindle' in the sentence given below. Rahul advised Neerja to appreciate or motivate her younger brother and not to dwindle or neglect his ideas all the time.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word 'dwindle' in the sentence given below.

Rahul advised Neerja to appreciate or motivate her younger brother and not to dwindle or neglect his ideas all the time.
questions.solution:
Dwindle - diminish gradually in size, amount, or strength.

Complement - to help make something or someone more complete or effective.

So, both words are opposite in meaning to each other.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Deprecate - express disapproval of.

Motivate - provide (someone) with a reason for doing something.

Neglect - fail to care for properly.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The bus is now full of passengers, it will leave soon.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The bus is now full of passengers, it will leave soon.
questions.solution:
When the plans are definite, then we should use 'is/are going to' in place of 'will'. So, the underlined phrase should be replaced with 'is going to leave'.

The correct sentence is: The bus is now full of passengers, it is going to leave soon.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Where was this pen found by him?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Where was this pen found by him?

options.text: Where do he find this pen?
options.html: Where do he find this pen?

options.text: Where does he find this pen?
options.html: Where does he find this pen?

options.text: Where did he found this pen?
options.html: Where did he found this pen?

options.text: Where did he find this pen?
options.html: Where did he find this pen?

questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

In Active voice (look at the options), it should be in interrogative form. These are "wh" questions that don't take "yes" or "no" as an answer.

"Which/ What/ Where" etc are placed as they are.

For example:

Where was this notebook hidden by him? (Passive)

Where did he hide this notebook? (Active)

The sentence in the Passive voice is in Simple Past tense. So, the sentence in the Active voice should be in Simple Past tense.

'Did' is always followed by the base verb, so option (c) is incorrect as 'found' is the past simple/past participle (V2/V3) form of the verb.

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Thus, the correct answer is option (d): Where did he find this pen?

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'. Kranthi loves to swim at the local swimming pool in order that relieve his work stress.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

Kranthi loves to swim at the local swimming pool in order that relieve his work stress.
questions.solution:
We use 'in order to' (and not 'in order that') with an infinitive form of a verb ('relieve' in this sentence) to express the purpose of something. The sentence discusses the purpose behind Kranthi going to swim at the local swimming pool.

So, the underlined phrase shall be replaced with the one in option (d).

The correct sentence is: Kranthi loves to swim at the local swimming pool in order to relieve his work stress.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Inherent
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Inherent
questions.solution:
Inherent - existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute.

Extraneous - not directly connected or related to a matter being considered.

So, both words are opposite in meaning to each other.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Natural - existing in or derived from nature; not made or caused by humankind.

Induce - succeed in persuading or leading (someone) to do something.

Restricted - limited in extent, number, scope, or action.

questions.question: Select the idiom from the given options that gives the most appropriate meaning of the highlighted text in the following sentence. A village fair is a place that contains many interesting objects . People of all age groups eagerly wait for this.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the idiom from the given options that gives the most appropriate meaning of the highlighted text in the following sentence.

A village fair is a place that contains many interesting objects. People of all age groups eagerly wait for this.
questions.solution:
Road to Damascus - used in reference to an important moment of insight, typically one that leads to a dramatic transformation of attitude or belief.

Usage: This might be a wake-up call for the Prime Minister - his road to Damascus.

Ivory tower - a state of privileged seclusion or separation from the facts and practicalities of the real world.

Usage: Academics sitting in ivory towers have no understanding of what is important for ordinary people.

Aladdin's cave - a place filled with a great number and variety of strange or precious items.

Usage: His shop, a veritable Aladdin's cave of antiques, is for sale.

Jewel in the crown - something that is the most valuable, important, or admired among others of its kind.

Usage: He owns several successful businesses but this company is the jewel in the crown.

As per the given meanings, only option (c) 'Aladdin's cave' best describes the village fair as a place that contains many interesting/precious/strange items.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. I named the child Ritesh.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

I named the child Ritesh.
questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

For example:

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): The child was named Ritesh.

questions.question: In the given sentence, one word may have been incorrectly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word from the given alternatives. If there is no error, select 'No error' as your answer. Decades of enimity between Lomovs and Chubukovs came to an end with the marriage between the two families.

In the given sentence, one word may have been incorrectly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word from the given alternatives. If there is no error, select 'No error' as your answer.

Decades of enimity between Lomovs and Chubukovs came to an end with the marriage between the two families.

questions.question: Select the correct direct form of the given sentence. She tells me that I am her lucky charm.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.

She tells me that I am her lucky charm.

options.text: She says to me, "You was my lucky charm."
options.html: She says to me, "You was my lucky charm."

options.text: She said to me, "You are my lucky charm."
options.html: She said to me, "You are my lucky charm."

options.text: She says to me, "I am your lucky charm."
options.html: She says to me, "I am your lucky charm."

options.text: She says to me, "You are my lucky charm."
options.html: She says to me, "You are my lucky charm."

questions.solution:
When the reporting verb in Indirect Speech is in Present Tense or Future Tense, there is no change in tense in Direct Speech. Though, the pronouns will change accordingly.

For Example:

Arnab says that he wants to be the best English teacher in India. (Indirect Speech)

Arnab says, "I want to be the best English teacher in India." (Direct Speech)

Subham will say that Kaustav is always late. (Indirect Speech)

Subham will say, "Kaustav is always late." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'Tells me' will be changed to 'says to me'.

The pronouns 'I' and 'her' will be changed to 'you' and 'my'.

'Am' will be changed to 'are'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (d): She says to me, "You are my lucky charm."

Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Chide
questions.solution:
Chide - scold or rebuke.

Prevent - keep (something) from happening.

Rescue - save (someone) from a dangerous or difficult situation.

Follow - go or come after (a person or thing proceeding ahead); move or travel behind.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The boy, as well as / his friends, were / absent from the class / when the teacher came.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The boy, as well as / his friends, were / absent from the class / when the teacher came.
questions.solution:
When words like along with, together with, as well as, accompanied by etc. are used to combine two subjects, the verb agrees with the subject mentioned first.

So, the verb 'were' (plural) does not agree with the first subject 'the boy' (singular). It should be replaced with the singular verb 'was'.

So, there is an error in part in option (c).

The correct sentence is: The boy, as well as his friends, was absent from the class when the teacher came.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order. Genome-wide P. with metabolites that influence Q. traits like flavour, disease resistance and texture R. analysis of each apple enabled S. identification of genetic markers associated
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

Genome-wide

P. with metabolites that influence

Q. traits like flavour, disease resistance and texture

R. analysis of each apple enabled

S. identification of genetic markers associated
questions.solution:
'Genome-wide' acts as an adjective which needs to be followed by a noun. So, option (a) is incorrect.

The verb 'associated' is always followed with the preposition 'with'. So, SP is a pair. So, option (b) is incorrect.

QR does not form a meaningful phrase. 'Texture analysis' is not a trait. So, option (d) is also eliminated.

So, the correct order is RSPQ.

The sentence thus formed is: Genome-wide analysis of each apple enabled identification of genetic markers associated with metabolites that influence traits like flavour, disease resistance and texture.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error. He describes the place vivid / that inspired in us / a wish to visit / the same.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.

He describes the place vivid / that inspired in us / a wish to visit / the same.
questions.solution:
The verb 'describes' requires an adverb to modify it, whereas 'vivid' is an adjective. Replacing 'vivid' with 'vividly' gives the meaning that 'he' described the place in such a clear manner which evoked strong wish in the speaker's heart to visit the same place.

The correct sentence is: He describes the place vividly that inspired in us a wish to visit the same.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.solution:
Motion - the action or process of moving or being moved.

Current - a body of water or air moving in a definite direction, especially through a surrounding body of water or air in which there is less movement.

Movement - the act or process of moving; especially : change of place or position or posture.

Fluctuation - an irregular rising and falling in number or amount; a variation.

As per the given meanings, the word 'movement' fits the best in context of the exercises.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.solution:
Yield - produce or provide (a natural, agricultural, or industrial product).

Attain - succeed in achieving (something that one has worked for).

Establish - set up on a firm or permanent basis.

Procure - obtain (something), especially with care or effort.

The sentence mentions a specific outcome out of exercising. Filling the blank with 'attain' gives the meaning that exercise is done to succeed in achieving a specific outcome. Other options do not fit in the context of the sentence.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.solution:
Magnifying - make (something) appear larger than it is, especially with a lens or microscope.

Amplifying - increase the volume of (sound), especially using an amplifier.

Intensifying - become or make more intense.

Enhancing - intensify, increase, or further improve the quality, value, or extent of.

The sentence discusses the aim of exercising with respect to fitness. Filling the blank with 'enhancing' gives the meaning that exercising is done in order to improve one's fitness.

Other options render the sentence meaningless.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.solution:
Lively - full of life and energy; active and outgoing.

Hectic - full of activity, or very busy.

Furious - extremely angry.

Feverish - characterized by or displaying a frenetic excitement or energy/ having or showing the symptoms of a fever.

The blank needs to be filled with an adjective that aptly modifies the noun 'day'. 'Furious' and 'feverish' are not apt adjectives for 'day'. The sentence implies that after the whole day, we tend towards leisure activities. So, it is after a hectic day that one would wish for leisure activities.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.solution:
Indulge - allow oneself to enjoy the pleasure of.

Luxuriate - enjoy (something) as a luxury; take self-indulgent delight in.

Abandon - cease to support or look after (someone); desert.

Coddle - treat (someone) in an indulgent or overprotective way.

The sentence implies the action/perception of the people towards leisure activities at the end of the day.

'Abandon' and 'coddle' do not fit in contextually.

The verb 'luxuriate' does not take 'in' after it.

Filling the blank with 'indulge' makes the sentence both contextually and grammatically correct.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.
